Class FailingCompilationVisitor

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.inject.visitor.rounds.FailingCompilationVisitor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Ordered, Toggleable, TypeElementVisitor<Object,Object>
public class FailingCompilationVisitor extends Object implements TypeElementVisitor<Object,Object>
Fails the compilation from finishCompilation(VisitorContext): with VisitorContext.fail(String, Element) for a class named "FailInFinishCompilation", and by throwing a ProcessingException for a class named "ThrowInFinishCompilation", whatever their package and language.

    • skipClassesGeneratedForOtherLanguages

      public boolean skipClassesGeneratedForOtherLanguages()
      Description copied from interface: TypeElementVisitor
      Whether javac should skip the Java representations of classes already visited by another language compiler.

      It currently covers Python: the Python compiler visits the Python classes with every visitor, then generates a Java class for each of them, which javac compiles in the same compilation. A visitor selected by an annotation never visits those Java classes, but a visitor of every class visits them again, for what the Python compiler added to them, unless it returns true here, for example because it contributes something for every class it visits and would otherwise contribute a Python class twice. The Java classes extending a Python class are not generated for it, and are visited in any case.

      Specified by:
      skipClassesGeneratedForOtherLanguages in interface TypeElementVisitor<Object,Object>
      Returns:
      Whether javac skips the Java classes generated for the classes of another language

    • finishCompilation

      public void finishCompilation(VisitorContext context)
      Description copied from interface: TypeElementVisitor
      Called once, after the last round of the compilation, when no class is visited anymore, before TypeElementVisitor.finish(VisitorContext).

      This is the point for work that has to see every class of the compilation, including the classes that another visitor or annotation processor generated as source in a later round: aggregating what every round visited, adding the beans that follow from it, and validating the result. A bean added here with VisitorContext.registerBean(ClassElement, io.micronaut.inject.ast.Element...) is written by every compiler, javac, KSP, Groovy and Python. A source generated here is not visited anymore.

      A visitor that implements this method has to return true from TypeElementVisitor.aggregatesCompilation(), so that the build knows before the compilation starts that the visitor has to see every class again whenever a class is changed, added or removed: an incremental compilation otherwise compiles the changed sources only, so the visitors would see only them, here as in every other method, and a visitor that writes nothing for the classes it saw would not be given the others in the next compilation. Everything written as a result of this method, the beans added here, their service entries, and the classes, sources and resources written here, follows from the whole compilation. A bean added here still has to be given the classes it follows from as originating elements:

      • javac: the annotation processor that runs a visitor aggregating the compilation is an aggregating processor for the incremental compilation of Gradle, registered for every class: Gradle processes again every class of the previous compilation, without compiling them again, whenever a source is changed, added or removed, and writes again everything the processor wrote. The files are written with every originating element, except to the filer of Gradle, which gets none: for a visitor that does not declare TypeElementVisitor.aggregatesCompilation(), whose processor stays isolating, such a file disables incremental annotation processing once it is written, which does not help a compilation that writes nothing.
      • KSP: the files are aggregating outputs of the files of their originating elements, which KSP writes again, processing those files again, whenever a source of the compilation is changed, added or removed. KSP has no way to declare a processor aggregating before it runs, so TypeElementVisitor.aggregatesCompilation() does not change it: until a visitor wrote something here, an incremental KSP compilation gives it the changed sources only. KSP also fixes the dependencies of a file when the GeneratedFile is obtained, so a file written here has to be obtained here, not kept from a round.
      • Groovy and Python: the originating elements are not reported to the build. Neither compiler tracks the origins of what the visitors write, and an incremental Python compilation visits the changed Python classes only.

      Where each compiler calls it:

      • javac: in the final annotation processing round, in which nothing generated is processed anymore. The bean definitions are written in that round, without javac warning that they are not processed. A source generated there is compiled, but javac warns that it is not processed.
      • KSP: from SymbolProcessor.finish. KSP invalidates the elements of a round when the round ends, so an element kept from a visit method or from TypeElementVisitor.finishRound(VisitorContext) must not be used here: look the classes up again by name, with VisitorContext.getClassElement(String), which resolves them anew.
      • Groovy: at class generation, after the last round.
      • Python: once for the Python classes, after their single round, on the visitors that visited them. javac then compiles the Java sources of the compilation and the Java classes generated for the Python classes, with other instances of the visitors, and calls it once more on those, as for any javac compilation. A visitor of every class also visits the Java classes generated for the Python classes there, unless it skips them with TypeElementVisitor.skipClassesGeneratedForOtherLanguages(), which a visitor that aggregates its classes here should do, so that it does not contribute a Python class twice.
